flaw: The done counter contradicts the standing decision three weeks ago that the printed account of open work carries no running total of finished rows, because a count that only grows answers nothing without a window nobody agreed on — and nothing since has reopened that decision.
what_you_do_next: Having said it plainly with the reason in the same reply, the pipeline proceeds rather than stalling: it finishes the decision sheet, admits the row through task-admission with the observable outcome and a definition of done a command can decide, opens the checkpoint for that goal, makes the three-line change in scripts/state-probe.sh, has a check that did not produce the work confirm the counter prints, closes checkpoint and row in the same step, and shows the result with what that part of the script said before, what it says now and what was added — so he can disagree while undoing it is still one revert.
reasoning: The execution reference makes this the one moment for the check: before the sheet turns into a checkpoint, the pipeline says so if it disagrees with the work itself, and a goal that conflicts with a standing decision already on record is named there as exactly such a flaw — stated plainly, with the reason, in the same reply that would otherwise just begin the work. Silent agreement is called out there as its own kind of failure, since the pipeline holds the fuller picture of what is already decided. The same clause forbids treating this as a question thrown back to stall: the pipeline still proceeds once heard out, on the human's word either way. Nothing here licenses waiting — the work is reversible, so rule 12's stop for a genuinely irreversible action does not apply, and a shown result closes the work without the human's eye as the gate on an ordinary delivery. His last clause is an instruction naming a goal nothing already covers, so it earns a sheet and creates exactly one row through the one write door; if he disagrees after seeing it, that is a new fact and its own task, not a reopening.
